headline: Pilbara Minerals craters 7.4% to close at $4.52 — the biggest story in your portfolio today — while the Middle East crisis keeps oil elevated and AI regulation is suddenly a hot-button issue in Washington.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: A rough session for Pilbara, dropping 7.4% to close at $4.52 — its worst single-day fall in recent memory. No specific news catalyst in today's feed, but lithium prices remain under sustained pressure as global EV demand growth slows and supply from new mines continues to weigh on spot prices. The stock is now down nearly 33% from your purchase price.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google popped 1.5% in last night's session to $335.45 USD, buoyed by fresh reporting that Alphabet's cloud division has hit a $514 billion order backlog after 82% revenue growth last quarter. Google Cloud is increasingly looking like a serious growth engine alongside Search, and the market liked it.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft edged up 0.65% last night to $495.63 USD. Azure's revenue figures are now being disclosed publicly for the first time, giving analysts more visibility into the cloud business. The stock continues to hold near all-time highs.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped a modest 0.69% last night to $215.47 USD — no major news catalyst. The stock remains below your purchase price overall, down about 7.2%, but there's nothing structurally alarming here. Long-term thesis (GTA VI cycle) remains intact.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI slipped a tiny 0.37% at today's ASX close to $16.25. Flat day, no specific news. The ETF is down about 14% from your entry — a reflection of the AI sector's choppy year rather than any single company issue.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged down 0.45% today to $75.66, tracking a broadly weak ASX session (the ASX 200 fell 0.89%). Nothing to read into — diversified fund, normal daily noise.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.15% today to $522.71, reflecting last night's solid US session (S&P 500 +0.86%, NASDAQ +0.96%). Your US total market exposure is now marginally in the green overall.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was dead flat today at $93.02. Emerging markets had no particular driver either way — the AUD ticked up slightly which can dampen returns on unhedged international holdings, but the effect here is negligible.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX) — big drop today, but hold steady
watch_today.detail: PLS fell 7.4% to $4.52 today — you're now down 33% on this position (-$49.41). There's no single news catalyst, but lithium's supply glut and soft EV demand are real headwinds. This is painful, but selling now locks in the loss. The long-term case for lithium in the energy transition is still intact — just taking longer than the market hoped. Sit tight unless your thesis has fundamentally changed.

watch_today.title: GOOG — strong momentum, cloud story getting louder
watch_today.detail: Alphabet gained 1.5% last night to $335.45 and the news behind it is genuinely compelling: Google Cloud's order backlog hit $514 billion after 82% revenue growth last quarter. That's not a fluke — cloud is becoming a second major growth engine alongside Search. You're up 9.1% on this position. Long-term, this is looking solid.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI regulation risk worth watching this week
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF is down 14% from entry and the regulatory environment is heating up. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft CEOs are all pushing Congress for new AI rules, and Obama is urging Democrats to make AI oversight a top priority. More regulation doesn't necessarily kill the sector — it can legitimise it — but watch for any hard legislative announcements that could spook AI-exposed stocks in the short term.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision coming — watch for ASX impact
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank is set to meet soon on interest rates, with a speech from RBA officials expected ahead of the decision. Markets are watching closely — any signal of a hold or cut would be good news for growth stocks and property-heavy ASX indices. A surprise hike (unlikely but possible given global inflation) would put further pressure on the ASX. Keep an eye on the language this week.

watch_today.title: Oil near $100 — Middle East tensions keeping prices elevated
watch_today.detail: Crude oil is sitting at $100.05 USD a barrel — right on that psychologically important level. Risks around the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea shipping lanes are keeping a floor under prices. Higher oil means higher petrol prices and broader cost-of-living pressure for everyday Australians. It also feeds into inflation, which can influence RBA decisions.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Azure revenue now publicly disclosed
watch_today.detail: Microsoft edged up 0.65% last night and a noteworthy structural change happened: Azure's revenue is now being disclosed publicly for the first time. This gives investors and analysts much better visibility into the cloud business. You're up 11.85% on this position — one of your best performers. Nothing to do here except hold.

world.summary: The Middle East dominates global headlines, with Iran-related tensions pushing oil toward a 4-month high and threatening shipping routes used by Australian importers. Meanwhile, the US political scene is a mixed bag of Trump drama, midterm manoeuvring, and Saudi Arabia caught in the crossfire.

stories.title: Oil hits 4-month high as Hormuz and Red Sea shipping risks mount
stories.why_it_matters: Oil has surged to a 4-month high, brushing $100 a barrel, as tensions around the Strait of Hormuz (the narrow chokepoint through which about 20% of the world's oil flows) and Red Sea shipping lanes continue to escalate. Iran and its allied militia groups are threatening vessels, making global shipping companies nervous. Higher oil prices flow directly into petrol prices at the bowser and push up the cost of goods transported by ship — which is most of what Australia imports.

stories.title: Middle East shipping escalation about to hit every Australian wallet
stories.why_it_matters: SBS is reporting that the Middle East shipping crisis is heading straight for Australian household budgets. Ships avoiding the Red Sea are being rerouted around Africa, adding weeks and thousands of dollars to journey times and costs. That means higher prices on everything from electronics and clothing to food — particularly products sourced from Europe and Asia. If the situation worsens, expect retailers to start passing those costs on within weeks.

stories.title: 'Worst case': Trump dealt major new blow in Iran conflict
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has suffered a significant setback in its Iran strategy, described by analysts as a 'worst case' scenario, though details remain limited in available reporting. The situation is fluid but underscores that US-Iran tensions are far from resolved. For markets, any escalation involving Iran carries the risk of oil supply disruption, which would push fuel costs higher globally.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia caught between Iran threats and limited options
stories.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia — the world's biggest oil exporter — is under mounting pressure from Iran and Iran-backed groups like the Houthis, and analysts say it has few good options to respond. If Saudi oil infrastructure gets targeted (as it has been in the past with drone strikes), that would be a serious shock to global oil supply and could send crude prices well above $100. That's the tail risk markets are quietly pricing in.

stories.title: Trump's $5,000 'dividend' plan faces funding questions ahead of US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Donald Trump is promising every American a $5,000 'dividend' payment if Republicans win the midterm elections — essentially a direct cash handout. But his own Commerce Secretary has admitted it can't be funded through tariff revenue alone, raising serious questions about where the money would come from (likely more government debt). If implemented, a massive unfunded stimulus like this could reignite US inflation, which would flow through to higher global interest rates and a stronger US dollar — relevant for anyone with USD-denominated assets.

markets.summary: The ASX had a rough Sunday session, falling 0.89% as investors digested global tensions and domestic uncertainty ahead of the RBA meeting. In contrast, last night's US session was solid — both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ gained on the back of strong tech earnings stories. Gold hit a new high above $4,400 USD an ounce, oil is hovering at $100, and the Aussie dollar ticked slightly higher.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Broad selloff today — weak sentiment driven by global uncertainty and pre-RBA nerves.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid session last night — tech strength and positive cloud earnings news drove gains.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech outperformed last night, helped by Google and Microsoft momentum.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil pulled back slightly from its 4-month high, but remains at the psychologically important $100 level amid Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold hit a new record high — investors seeking safe havens amid geopolitical uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar nudged up slightly — traders slightly more confident the RBA won't hike aggressively.

politics.summary: The RBA's crucial interest rate meeting is on the horizon, with officials set to speak ahead of the decision. Meanwhile, Labor is copping criticism from within its own ranks over falling house prices and real wages, and the government has quietly ditched a significant plastic packaging reform — sparking backlash from environmental groups.

stories.title: RBA to speak ahead of crucial cash rate meeting
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank is holding a critical interest rate meeting imminently, with RBA officials scheduled to make public remarks beforehand — a signal they may be preparing the market for a decision. Australians with mortgages are watching closely. Any cut would bring mortgage relief; a hold keeps the pressure on; a hike (unlikely but not impossible) would be a shock. The outcome will also directly affect the ASX, particularly interest-rate-sensitive sectors like property and banking.

stories.title: 'Don't insult me': Labor luminary unleashes over falling house prices and real wages
stories.why_it_matters: A prominent Labor figure has broken ranks to publicly criticise the Albanese government over falling house prices and stagnant real wages (wages that aren't keeping up with inflation). The outburst signals internal frustration within Labor that the economic recovery isn't reaching everyday Australians. Falling house prices are good news for first-home buyers but painful for existing homeowners — and the political optics for Labor ahead of any future election are getting harder.

stories.title: Labor ditches new packaging laws to cut plastic waste, drawing widespread criticism
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government has quietly shelved proposed laws that would have required companies to use more sustainable packaging and reduce single-use plastic waste. Environmental and industry groups — including those who had already invested in compliance — are furious, with one group calling it an 'unprecedented scale and breadth of outrage'. The reversal appears to be a cost-of-living concession, as new packaging requirements add costs that businesses pass on to consumers, but critics say it's a significant step backward on environmental commitments.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant story this weekend — the CEOs of the world's biggest AI companies are voluntarily asking governments to impose rules on them, while Barack Obama is pushing Democrats to make AI oversight a central political issue. Separately, Google's latest AI model is getting strong benchmark results at a fraction of competitor costs.

stories.title: OpenAI and Anthropic CEOs propose an 'AI development brake' mechanism
stories.why_it_matters: The CEOs of OpenAI (Sam Altman) and Anthropic (Dario Amodei) — the two most powerful AI labs in the world — are jointly proposing a mechanism that would allow governments or regulators to 'put the brakes' on AI development if it starts moving too fast or shows dangerous signs. This is remarkable: the companies building the most powerful AI are asking to be regulated. It suggests the people closest to the technology are genuinely worried about where it's heading, and are trying to get ahead of potential disasters.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft CEOs ask Congress to mandate synthetic DNA screening
stories.why_it_matters: In a rare show of unity, the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Microsoft jointly appeared before Congress to urge mandatory screening of synthetic DNA — artificial genetic code that AI can now help design. The concern is that AI tools could be used to help bad actors engineer dangerous pathogens. This is a biosecurity issue as much as an AI issue, and the fact that tech CEOs are proactively pushing for this kind of regulation signals how seriously the industry is taking worst-case scenarios.

stories.title: Obama urges Democrats to put AI oversight at the centre of their agenda
stories.why_it_matters: Barack Obama has made a high-profile push for Democrats to prioritise AI regulation as a top political issue heading into the 2026 midterms. He's arguing the party that gets ahead of AI governance will have a significant political advantage. This matters for markets because it signals bipartisan momentum toward real regulation — which could mean compliance costs for tech companies, but also stability and legitimacy for the sector long-term.

stories.title: Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash model scores within 2 points of Claude Opus 4.7 at one-third the cost
stories.why_it_matters: Google's latest AI model — Gemini 3.5 Flash — is scoring nearly as well as Anthropic's top-tier Claude Opus 4.7 on standard benchmark tests, but at about a third of the price. In practical terms, this means businesses using AI can get near-top-quality results much more cheaply if they switch to Google's model. It's a significant competitive move by Google and good news for your GOOG holding — it shows Alphabet is keeping pace with (and undercutting) rivals on price.

stories.title: NYT: Inside the doomsday discussions happening at AI companies right now
stories.why_it_matters: The New York Times has published a detailed look inside the private conversations happening at AI companies about what they call 'superintelligence doomsday' scenarios — situations where AI becomes too powerful for humans to control or correct. The fact that these conversations are now leaking publicly tells you just how seriously insiders are taking the risks. It adds context to why AI CEOs are proactively seeking regulation rather than fighting it.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 1 is done and dusted — the Knights, Dolphins, Sharks and Panthers all advance. In AFL, Taylor Walker played his final game and the tributes are flowing, while the Broncos' recruitment of Lote Gagai is drawing attention for the finals push.

stories.title: Panthers 19 def. Roosters 12 — Penrith advance in controversial finish
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith Panthers defeated the Sydney Roosters 19-12 in today's Finals Week 1 clash at CommBank Stadium. The game had talking points aplenty — Nathan Cleary copped a sin bin (10 minutes off the field for foul play), Roosters coach Trent Robinson was criticised for a major tactical mistake, and Elliott Yeo was a key figure. The Panthers advance to the next finals round while the Roosters' season is over.

stories.title: Dolphins 26 def. Warriors 16 — historic Dolphins finals win
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins made history on Saturday, defeating the Warriors 26-16 at Go Media Stadium in Auckland in what Fox Sports called a 'fiery finals thriller'. The Dolphins are a relatively new club and this victory is a significant milestone in their short history. The Warriors, playing at home, were stunned into silence — a tough result for their fans. Warriors: eliminated. Dolphins: into the next round.

stories.title: Sharks 26 def. Cowboys 16 — Trindall's heroic return
stories.why_it_matters: The Cronulla Sharks beat the North Queensland Cowboys 26-16 on Saturday night, with halfback Nicho Hynes-rival Braydon Trindall making a remarkable return from a shoulder dislocation to lead the team in the finals win. Trindall's comeback was seen as a huge lift for Cronulla. The Cowboys' season ends here; the Sharks march on.

stories.title: Taylor Walker plays final AFL game — tributes pour in
stories.why_it_matters: Adelaide Crows veteran Taylor Walker has played his final AFL game, with the AFL world rallying around the Hawthorn star in what were described as 'devastating' scenes. Dayne Zorko of the Lions was praised for a heartfelt gesture toward Walker after the game. Walker has been a key figure in Adelaide's identity for over a decade — his retirement marks the end of an era for the Crows.
